text:
I will estimate the causal effect of holding a microloan by using the randomized 2007 extra-officer assignment, officer_slots, as an instrument for the household’s microloan indicator.
The sample will be restricted to branch_area neighborhoods, where officer_slots is observed and branch-area direct effects, including the business-skills course, are common to both instrument arms.
The first stage will use officer_slots to predict the microloan indicator, reporting the first-stage F statistic, predicted loan probability, and compliance.
The second stage will regress the documented follow-up monthly business-profit measure on the predicted microloan, with standard errors clustered by neighborhood or branch and baseline covariates used only for balance checks.
This identifies the local average treatment effect for branch-area households whose loan status is induced by extra staffing, not a uniform effect for all possible loans.
The main threat is exclusion, because extra officers might affect profits through processing speed, service quality, monitoring, or advice independent of loan receipt, so I will check baseline balance and placebo outcomes.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Restrict to the 52 branch neighborhoods and use officer_slots, the randomized extra loan-officer staffing, as an instrument for household microloan take-up.
Estimate a 2SLS LATE of loan on monthly business profits, instrumented by officer_slots, with standard errors clustered by neighborhood and a reported first-stage F.
Key variables are officer_slots, the loan treatment, and monthly business profits.
The main threat is exclusion: officer_slots must affect profits only by changing loan uptake, while branch_area is not usable because the free business-skills course can directly raise profits.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would use a randomized encouragement design within the 52 branch neighborhoods, instrumenting household microloan with officer_slots.
officer_slots is a credible instrument because the 2007 staffing pilot is randomly assigned within branch areas, raises loan uptake by 12 percentage points, and officers only process loan applications.
I would first stage loan on officer_slots plus baseline controls, then run 2SLS predicting monthly business profits from loan with neighborhood-clustered standard errors, reporting the LATE for branch-area households induced to borrow.
I would not use branch_area as the instrument because the business-skills course in branch areas may affect profits directly.
The key variables are officer_slots, the household loan indicator, monthly business profits, branch_area for the sample restriction, and baseline controls such as hh_size, head_educ, assets, slum, dist_market, and biz_2005.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Estimate the local average effect of holding a microloan, among branch-area households whose loan take-up is increased by the extra officer, using two-stage least squares with officer_slots as the instrument for the household loan indicator.
Restrict the sample to branch_area=1, where officer_slots is defined, and cluster standard errors by neighborhood/branch because the instrument is assigned at the branch level.
Include baseline household covariates (hh_size, head_educ, biz_2005, assets) for precision and check balance of officer_slots against slum and dist_market.
The first stage regresses the loan indicator on officer_slots; the second stage regresses deflated monthly business profits on the predicted loan.
Do not use branch_area as the instrument, because the free business-skills course in branch neighborhoods violates exclusion by directly affecting profits.
The main threat is exclusion violation if the extra officer also affects profits through loan terms, advice, or screening rather than only changing loan take-up.

CANDIDATES:
officer_slots | plausible
branch_area | violated
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Estimate the effect of the household microloan indicator on follow-up monthly profits with a randomized-encouragement 2SLS design, using officer_slots as the instrument because it increases loan take-up by 12 percentage points.
Restrict to households in the 52 branch neighborhoods where officer_slots is randomly assigned and cluster standard errors by neighborhood.
The key variables are branch_area to define the sample, officer_slots, the microloan indicator, follow-up business profits, and baseline covariates such as biz_2005, assets, head_educ, slum, dist_market, and hh_size.
The 2SLS coefficient is the LATE for households whose loan decision is changed by extra branch staffing.
The main threat is the free business-skills course in branch neighborhoods, which can raise profits without a loan and therefore invalidates branch_area as an instrument.
I will rely on officer_slots, whose only stated role is loan processing, and view any non-loan effect of extra staffing as the remaining exclusion risk.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Use a fuzzy randomized-assignment IV design in the 52 branch areas, instrumenting microloan receipt with officer_slots, the randomized extra loan officer. The key variables are officer_slots, the microloan indicator, and deflated three-year monthly business profits, with neighborhood-clustered standard errors and baseline covariates such as biz_2005, head_educ, assets, slum, and dist_market only for precision. The first stage should recover the documented 12-point loan increase, and the reduced-form profit effect divided by that first stage gives the LATE for loans induced by officer staffing. The main threat is the city's free business-skills course in branch areas, which invalidates branch_area as an instrument, while officer_slots' remaining concern is weak first-stage power from a neighborhood-level 12-point shock.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would estimate the effect of actually holding a microloan with a two-stage least squares design, using officer_slots as the instrument and restricting to the 52 branch neighborhoods.
The first stage would include officer_slots, baseline business status, assets, household size, head education, slum status, and market distance; the second stage would regress monthly business profits on the predicted microloan indicator.
I would cluster standard errors by neighborhood and interpret the result as a LATE for branch-neighborhood households whose loan receipt is induced by the officer assignment.
The main threat is that extra officers or associated branch changes might affect profits through non-lending services or local spillovers, rather than only through loans.
This design avoids the branch_area threat because the city's business-skills course was assigned to all branch neighborhoods and could directly raise profits.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Restrict the analysis to branch_area = 1, use loan_indi_128 as the endogenous microloan indicator, and use busine_amou_038 as the follow-up monthly business profit outcome.
Use officer_slots, the randomized extra-loan-officer assignment within branch areas, as the instrument because it changes only loan processing and therefore affects profits only through microloan take-up.
The first stage uses officer_slots to predict loan_indi_128, and the reduced form compares busine_amou_038 across officer_slots = 1 and 0 branches, supported by the 12-percentage-point loan-rate gap.
Estimate the LATE by 2SLS/Wald, with baseline hh_size, head_educ, assets, biz_2005, slum, and dist_market as precision controls and standard errors clustered by neighborhood.
Do not use branch_area as the instrument because branch assignment also induces the separate business-skills course, violating exclusion; this design identifies the local effect of actually holding a microloan among branch-area compliers.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Within the 52 branch-area households, estimate the LATE of microloan receipt (loan_indi_040) on follow-up business profits (busine_amou_038) by two-stage least squares, using officer_slots as the instrument for loan take-up. Control for baseline characteristics hh_size, head_educ, biz_2005, assets, slum, and dist_market, and use neighborhood-clustered standard errors. Do not use branch_area as the instrument because the free business-skills course in every branch neighborhood is a direct profit channel; the main threat to officer_slots is exclusion failure through non-loan channels or a small, local first stage.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I will use the 2007 randomized extra loan-officer slot in branch neighborhoods as an encouragement instrument for whether a household holds a microloan, estimating the LATE of loan holding on deflated monthly business profits.
The first stage will be a neighborhood-clustered linear probability model of the loan-status indicator on officer_slots, and the second stage will instrument loan status in the profit equation.
The analysis sample will be the 52 branch neighborhoods, with key variables officer_slots, a validated loan-status indicator, and the deflated three-year-follow-up business-profit outcome.
I will include baseline business, assets, education, slum, market distance, and household size only for precision, after checking balance on officer_slots.
I will report neighborhood-cluster standard errors, first-stage F, and weak-instrument-robust intervals, with branch_area intention-to-treat as a robustness check.
The main threat is that officer_slots could affect profits through channels other than the household's binary loan, such as loan size, terms, monitoring, or local branch effects.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | doubtful
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would estimate the local effect of holding a microloan by two-stage least squares, instrumenting the household loan indicator with officer_slots from the randomized 2007 staffing pilot and clustering by neighborhood. officer_slots affects loan access through application-processing capacity, and the documentation says loan officers only process applications, so it plausibly satisfies exclusion. The key variables are officer_slots, the binary microloan treatment, the three-year business-profit outcome, and branch_area only to define the 52-neighborhood branch subpopulation and check balance. The main threat to the obvious branch_area IV is the city business-skills course, which violates exclusion; my chosen officer_slots IV avoids that but is weaker.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would estimate the local average effect of a household microloan for branch-area compliers on monthly business profit using two-stage least squares in the 52 branch neighborhoods, with officer_slots instrumenting household loan status. The key variables are officer_slots, the household loan indicator, the three-year business-profit outcome, and branch_area for restricting to branches where the staffing pilot is defined. The first stage is loan status on officer_slots and the IV estimate is the ratio of the officer_slots reduced-form effect on profit to that first stage, with standard errors clustered by neighborhood. I would not use branch_area as an instrument because the free business-skills course in priority wards can directly affect profits, violating its exclusion restriction. The main threat is that extra officers may affect profits through local loan markets, group-lending spillovers, or other branch services rather than only through the household’s own loan.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I will estimate the loan effect with 2SLS among the 52 branch areas, using officer_slots as the instrument for the household microloan indicator.
The outcome is deflated 2009 monthly business profits, with controls for hh_size, head_educ, biz_2005, assets, slum, and dist_market, and neighborhood-clustered standard errors.
officer_slots is the randomized extra-officer assignment, and its plausibility rests on officers only processing loan applications.
The main threat is the free business-skills course in every 2006 priority ward, which invalidates branch_area, and the remaining threat to officer_slots is non-loan channels such as loan terms or spillovers.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I will not use branch_area because the free business-skills course in branch neighborhoods can affect profits directly, violating the exclusion restriction. Instead, I will restrict to the 52 branch neighborhoods and use randomized officer_slots as a 2SLS instrument for the binary microloan indicator, estimating a neighborhood-clustered LATE. Key variables are officer_slots, the binary microloan indicator, real monthly follow-up business profits in rupees, and baseline controls such as biz_2005, assets, head_educ, and hh_size. The main threat is that the extra officer affects profits through non-credit channels, so I will check first-stage strength, pre-treatment business outcomes, and sensitivity to exclusion violations.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Restrict to the 52 branch areas and use officer_slots as an instrument for the microloan treatment indicator, because the 2007 extra-officer pilot is randomized and, per the documentation, affects profits only through loan processing.
Estimate a first stage of the loan indicator on officer_slots with baseline controls (biz_2005, assets, head_educ, hh_size, slum, dist_market), and a second stage of the 2009 business-profit outcome on the predicted loan, yielding a LATE for branch-area compliers.
Cluster by neighborhood and use wild-cluster bootstrap; treat branch_area only as an ITT robustness check because the service-area business-skills course may directly affect profits.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Among branch_area households, use the randomized officer_slots staffing pilot as an instrument for the binary microloan indicator in a 2SLS model of business profits three years after branch opening. officer_slots is relevant because it raises loan take-up by 12 percentage points and, per the memo, loan officers only process applications, so it should affect profits only through loan receipt. I will report the first stage, estimate the local effect for officer-induced borrowers, and cluster standard errors by neighborhood, with biz_2005, head_educ, assets, slum, and dist_market used only for balance and diagnostics. I will not use branch_area as the instrument because the co-located free business-skills course gives it a direct path to business profits.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would estimate the loan effect by 2SLS among the 52 branch neighborhoods, using officer_slots as the instrument for loan receipt (loan_indi_128) and follow-up business profits (busine_amou_258) as the outcome, with neighborhood-clustered standard errors and a first-stage F statistic.
I would not use branch_area as the instrument because the city business-skills course was delivered in the same service areas and could directly affect profits or loan demand, violating the exclusion restriction.
officer_slots is the more credible instrument because the staffing pilot was randomized within branch areas and loan officers are documented to only process applications, so the main channel should be loan receipt.
The main threat is that extra officers could still affect profits through faster processing, counseling, or different loan terms, and the estimate remains a local effect for branch-area compliers with only about 52 clusters.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

Use officer_slots as an instrumental variable for the household's microloan indicator, exploiting the lender's 2007 randomized extra-officer staffing shock. Use branch_area to restrict the analysis to the 52 branch neighborhoods, where the city business-skills course tied to branch assignment is constant, and include baseline controls (hh_size, head_educ, biz_2005, assets, slum, dist_market). The first stage regresses the loan indicator on officer_slots and these controls. The second stage regresses monthly business profits on the predicted loan indicator, with standard errors clustered by neighborhood. This yields the LATE of a microloan for branch-neighborhood households whose loan uptake changes because of the extra officer. The main threat is exclusion failure if the staffing pilot also changed outreach, loan terms, or other services that directly affect profits.
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I would report the officer_slots 2SLS estimate, -968 rupees, with a 95% confidence interval of [-3146, 1210]. This is a LATE for branch-area households affected by the randomized extra loan officer. branch_area is invalid because the free business-skills course was targeted to the same service areas and can affect profits directly, while officer_slots plausibly affects profits only through loan take-up.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
ESTIMATE: -968
CI: -3146, 1210
METHOD: 2SLS LATE using officer_slots

Do not use branch_area as an instrument, because the city's business-skills course was tied to the same service areas and can directly affect business profits. Instead, I would restrict to the 52 branch-area neighborhoods and use the randomized 2007 officer_slots as an instrument for the household microloan indicator. The 2SLS/LATE model would regress 2009 monthly business profits on the loan indicator, instrumented by officer_slots, with baseline controls (hh_size, head_educ, biz_2005, assets, slum, dist_market) and standard errors clustered by branch/neighborhood. This identifies the local effect of households induced to take a microloan by an extra officer, since the staffing pilot is randomized and officers only process applications. The main threat is weak and local identification: the first stage is 12 points, the instrument is branch-area only, and cluster-level inference uses 52 neighborhoods.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

The branch-area instrument is contaminated because the free business-skills course was offered in all service areas, so branch_area has a direct path to business profits.
The 2007 staffing pilot randomized extra officers within branch areas and, per the memo, only changed loan application processing, making officer_slots a plausible instrument.
I therefore report the 2SLS LATE for branch-area households whose loan status the extra officer shifts: -2838 rupees per month.
The 95% confidence interval is -5286 to -390 rupees per month.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
ESTIMATE: -2838
CI: -5286, -390
METHOD: 2SLS LATE using officer_slots

Use officer_slots, the randomized 2007 extra-officer shock, because it is random within branch areas and should affect profits only by changing the probability of holding a microloan. Branch_area is not a valid instrument for the loan effect because the city’s business-skills course was also assigned to those same service areas and could directly affect profits. Officer_slots therefore identifies a local loan effect for branch-area households, which is the cleanest causal estimate available.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
ESTIMATE: 369
CI: -2112, 2850
METHOD: 2SLS LATE using officer_slots

I would report the officer_slots 2SLS estimate rather than OLS or branch_area, because officer assignment was randomized within branch areas and is strongly relevant. Branch_area is invalid here because the city's business-skills course was offered in those service areas and can directly affect profits, violating exclusion. Officer_slots is plausible because loan officers only process loan applications, so the extra officer likely affects profits only through loan receipt. The resulting estimate is a local average treatment effect for branch-area households whose microloan take-up is shifted by the staffing pilot. It is -2,006 rupees, with a 95% CI of [-4,627, 615].
CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
ESTIMATE: -2006
CI: -4627, 615
METHOD: 2SLS IV using officer_slots (LATE)

I would report the 2SLS estimate using the randomized extra loan officer, not the branch-area IV. Officer slots are strongly relevant and have a credible exclusion restriction because the extra officer only changes loan processing. Branch area is a less credible instrument for a household’s own loan because a new branch may directly affect neighborhood business profits and was placed subject to an eligibility rule. The officer-based estimate identifies the local effect of taking a microloan in branch areas. Its normal 95% confidence interval is 393 ± 1.96×1,305.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | doubtful
officer_slots | plausible
ESTIMATE: 393
CI: -2165, 2951
METHOD: 2SLS using officer_slots

I would not use ballot_drawn as an instrument because the free training course assigned to all drawn applicants directly affects income; instead, I would run an IV/LATE design within ballot-drawn applicants.
The instrument is fare_pilot, the random airfare-pilot assignment among drawn applicants, and the endogenous treatment is migration within two years.
The key variables are fare_pilot, the migration indicator, the observed weekly income outcome three years after the ballot in New Zealand dollars, ballot-year fixed effects, and pre-application covariates such as age, female, educ, income_app, employed_app, and hh_size.
The first stage regresses migration on fare_pilot, using the reported 25-percentage-point first-stage effect.
The second stage regresses the income outcome on predicted migration to estimate the local causal effect of migration for drawn applicants.
The main threat is that the pilot assignment violates exclusion if it affects income through channels other than migration.

CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

I would estimate a local average treatment effect of migration for drawn applicants using two-stage least squares with the random airfare pilot (fare_pilot) as an instrument for migration within two years, restricted to ballot_drawn = 1 and with ballot-year fixed effects. The first stage regresses migration on fare_pilot; the reduced form regresses three-year weekly income on fare_pilot, and their ratio identifies the causal effect for drawn applicants who migrate because of the pilot. Key variables are fare_pilot, ballot_drawn, migration within two years, three-year weekly income, ballot-year, and baseline precision controls such as age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size. The main threat is exclusion: the airfare pilot or being chosen for it may affect income through non-migration channels, such as direct financial effects, changed job search or remittance behavior, or differential attrition.

CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

I would use the fare_pilot random encouragement among drawn applicants as the instrument for migration, rather than ballot_drawn, because the mandatory post-draw training gives ballot_drawn a direct effect on income.
I would estimate a two-stage least squares encouragement model on the drawn sample with ballot-year fixed effects and baseline controls (age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, hh_size), where the reduced form on the three-year weekly-income outcome identifies a LATE for winners whose migration is induced by the airfare subsidy.
The main threat is exclusion: the pilot must not influence income through non-migration channels such as differential training completion, counseling, or liquidity effects.

CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

Within applicants with ballot_drawn = 1, use fare_pilot as a randomized instrument for migration within two years and estimate a two-stage least-squares local average effect. The instrument has a first stage of about 25 percentage points, with ballot-year fixed effects absorbing annual quota and New Zealand labor-market shocks. Pre-ballot covariates age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size are included as balance and efficiency controls, not as the identifying restriction. Restricting to drawn applicants holds the free trade-certificate course constant, because the course is assigned to all drawn applicants and would otherwise invalidate ballot_drawn through a direct income channel. Estimate the reduced form of fare_pilot on three-year weekly income in New Zealand dollars, with sensitivity checks for any direct effect of the paid airfare. Use robust standard errors clustered by ballot-year, interpreting the estimate as the effect of migrating for drawn applicants who migrate because of the pilot.

CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

Estimate the local effect of migration among drawn applicants by 2SLS, using fare_pilot to instrument the two-year migration indicator because the airfare pilot was randomly assigned among drawn applicants and raises take-up by 25 points.
Key variables are fare_pilot, the two-year migration indicator, three-year weekly income, ballot_drawn to define the drawn sample, and baseline controls age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size.
I would use ballot-year fixed effects, cluster standard errors by ballot year, and report the first-stage F.
The main threat is exclusion: the pilot must affect income only by changing migration.
The estimate is a LATE for drawn applicants, not all applicants.

CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

Restrict to drawn applicants and use a randomized-encouragement IV design, instrumenting the two-year migration indicator with fare_pilot, the random airfare-pilot assignment.
It is relevant because pilot applicants are 25 percentage points more likely to migrate, while the universal training course makes ballot_drawn non-excludable.
Run a first stage of migration on fare_pilot with ballot-year fixed effects, then an IV regression of follow-up weekly income on migration, using age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size only for precision.
The estimate is the LATE for drawn applicants whose migration is changed by the airfare.
The main threat is that fare_pilot may affect income through non-migration channels, such as temporary travel, job search, or attrition.
CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

I would restrict the analysis to drawn applicants and use fare_pilot as a randomized encouragement to instrument the migration treatment in a model for weekly income three years after the ballot.
The key variables are ballot_drawn to define the drawn sample, fare_pilot, migration, weekly income, ballot-year fixed effects, and baseline controls age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size.
The first stage is the documented 25-point increase in migration for pilot applicants, and the estimand is the local average effect of migration for drawn applicants whose migration is induced by the pilot.
I would not use ballot_drawn as the instrument because the free trade course for all drawn applicants creates a non-migration path from draw to income.
The main threat is that the pilot affects income through channels other than migration, such as direct travel benefits or altered expectations, which would violate the exclusion restriction.
CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

Use a two-stage least squares encouragement design, restricting to drawn applicants and instrumenting migration within two years with fare_pilot, a random airfare subsidy. fare_pilot increases migration by 25 percentage points, so the reduced form identifies a local average treatment effect for drawn compliers. In the first stage regress migration on fare_pilot, ballot-year fixed effects, and baseline controls (age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, hh_size); in the second stage regress three-year weekly income on predicted migration with the same controls. Report the first-stage F statistic and 2SLS estimates with robust standard errors. I will not use ballot_drawn because all drawn applicants receive the free trade-certificate course, giving the draw a direct income channel. The main threat is that fare_pilot may have a direct effect on income or that the estimate applies only to drawn compliers.

fare_pilot | plausible

I will estimate a local average effect of migration on three-year weekly income among drawn applicants using a randomized encouragement design in a 2SLS/Wald framework.
I will use fare_pilot as the instrument for migration within two years, with ballot-year fixed effects and pre-ballot age, sex, schooling, employment, income, and household size for precision.
I will not use ballot_drawn because all drawn applicants receive a trade-certificate course that can directly affect income.

fare_pilot | plausible

I would use fare_pilot, a randomly assigned airfare subsidy among drawn applicants, as an instrumental variable for migration rather than the raw ballot draw.
The random-encouragement IV/LATE identifies the effect of actually migrating on three-year weekly income for drawn applicants whose migration decision is induced by the pilot.
I would restrict the sample to drawn applicants, include ballot-year fixed effects, and control for pre-ballot variables age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size.
The first stage would regress migration within two years on fare_pilot and the same controls; 2SLS would then use predicted migration to estimate the outcome effect.
I would reject ballot_drawn as an instrument because every drawn applicant received a free trade-certificate course that can directly affect later income.
I would report the first-stage F-statistic, covariate-balance diagnostics, and a placebo test using income_app to support the exclusion restriction.

CANDIDATES:

fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

I will identify the local effect of migration on weekly income by using fare_pilot, the randomly assigned airfare subsidy among drawn applicants, as an instrument for migration within two years.
I will estimate it only within ballot_drawn = 1, because ballot_drawn itself is likely invalid: all drawn applicants are placed on the skills roll and receive a trade-certificate course that may directly affect income.
The key variables are fare_pilot, migration within two years, three-year weekly income in New Zealand dollars, and baseline controls age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size.
I will add ballot-year fixed effects, first regressing migration on fare_pilot and the baseline controls to test the first stage.
Then I will regress the income outcome on the instrumented migration variable with the same controls and year fixed effects, yielding the LATE for drawn applicants whose migration is induced by the pilot.
The main threat is exclusion failure, if pilot status affects income through job-search, signaling, timing, or labor-market channels other than migration.
CANDIDATES:

fare_pilot | plausible
INSTRUMENT: fare_pilot

I would use two-stage least squares among drawn applicants, instrumenting migration within two years with fare_pilot, the random airfare subsidy, and including weekly income three years after the ballot, ballot-year fixed effects, and baseline controls (age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, hh_size).
This estimates a local average effect for drawn applicants whose migration is induced by the pilot.
I would not use ballot_drawn because it directly affects income through the free trade-certificate course given to everyone on the successful-applicant register.
The main threat to the chosen instrument is that the airfare payment could affect income through non-migration channels, such as settlement finances or timing.
I would test this with placebo outcomes and report first-stage and reduced-form results.
CANDIDATES:
ballot_drawn | violated
fare_pilot | plausible

Use fare_pilot as an IV for actual migration within the drawn subsample, because it is randomly assigned among drawn applicants and increases migration by 25 percentage points.
Assume the airfare subsidy affects three-year income only by enabling migration.
Include baseline age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size, plus ballot-year fixed effects, with robust standard errors.
Reject ballot_drawn as an instrument because all drawn applicants received a free trade-certificate course that can directly affect income.
Estimate the 2SLS LATE of migration on weekly income for drawn compliers, reporting first-stage F and weak-instrument-robust inference.

Within drawn applicants, use a two-stage least squares design in which the random fare_pilot assignment instruments the treatment, migration within two years.
Regress the outcome, weekly income three years after the ballot, on migration and pre-ballot controls age, female, educ, employed_app, income_app, and hh_size, with ballot-year fixed effects.
The first stage should show that fare_pilot raises migration, identifying a local effect for drawn applicants induced to migrate.
